newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech firms see 1996 trade gap topping CZK 160 bln.
newsitem.headline: Czech firms see 1996 trade gap topping CZK 160 bln.

text.p: Czech foreign trade firms expect the country's 1996 trade deficit to grow to 163 billion crowns from the seven-month total of 85.3 billion crowns, a government survey showed on Monday.
The Czech Statistical Bureau's survey of foreign-trade companies found an average expectation of import growth for the full year of 16.5 percent to total 781 billion crowns for the year.
That compares with an average expectation of seven percent growth in exports to total 618 billion crowns.

The country posted a 1995 trade deficit of 95.7 billion crowns, and through seven months in 1996 the trade deficit for the year was 85.3 billion crowns, compared with a 49.5 billion crown deficit for the same period last year.
The seven-month total came with a record single-month deficit of 16.4 billion crowns in July.
The bureau said its survey was sent to 170 firms, and 64 percent of those answered the survey.
But it said the survey averages are more pessimistic than the CSU's own earlier forecast of a 143 billion crown 1996 trade deficit
